newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sets date for NATO vote.
newsitem.headline: Spain sets date for NATO vote.

text.p: Spain's parliament will vote November 14 on whether to fully integrate into NATO's military structure, a government official said on Tuesday.

Spain, a member of the 16-nation alliance, opted in a 1986 referendum to stay out of the integrated military command. But Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has said he is confident that parliament will back him and agree to full integration.
He said circumstances had changed radically since 1986 with the end of the Cold War and NATO's decision to allow European allies to use NATO equipment and resources for their own operations.
As a condition of joining the military command, Spain has said it should a NATO command over the Straits of Gibraltar and all of Iberia.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, a former Spanish foreign minister, pledged last month to try to "bring about the conditions Spain seeks for its full integration."
Socialist opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez has said he will support the government on the NATO issue.
